description: Trigger and behavior cases for mobile journey QA design: critical journeys with a mobile check matrix (breakpoints, touch, dialogs, navigation, orientation, keyboard, safe area), a device + data matrix, evidence composition via screenshot-evidence-planner, and routing away from layout correctness, live execution, spec implementation, and per-change plans.

cases.prompt: Design mobile journey QA for our invoicing app — which critical journeys to verify on phones, and what mobile-specific checks does each journey need?

assertions: Names the critical journeys with a why-critical reason each.
Enumerates the mobile-specific check matrix per journey: breakpoints, touch, dialogs, navigation, orientation, keyboard, safe area.
Names the device/viewport + data matrix and states evidence follows screenshot-evidence-planner conventions.
Designs journey checks without redesigning the layout, and claims to drive nothing.

cases.prompt: Two of our journeys only differ at the 320px breakpoint. What mobile QA do they need?

assertions: Names the 320px-specific checks those journeys need (touch targets, safe area, dialogs) instead of duplicating the full matrix for every journey.
Keeps layout fitting and viewport correctness with mobile-viewport-craft rather than absorbing it.

cases.prompt: Fix the 100vh layout bug on phones — the footer overlaps the browser chrome.

assertions: Does not invoke this skill; layout and viewport correctness design belongs to mobile-viewport-craft.
Halts and asks for the journey or route inventory before designing coverage.
Does not invent journeys from the product name.

cases.prompt: Design the mobile journey coverage for checkout, then run the pass on a real phone.

assertions: Produces the coverage design, then stops at execution: running the pass is clickthrough-test-engineer (manual-only) or playwright-e2e-engineer (manual-only) and is handed off by name, not executed in the same pass.
States the handoff explicitly rather than silently dropping the execution half of the ask.

cases.prompt: Design the mobile journey checks for a 73-entry guide list on a 390x844 phone: search/filter, select a deep named entry, inspect its detail, return to the list. Include what can go wrong when adjacent records look alike.

assertions: Specifies select -> inspect detail -> return for the journey, recording the visible selected row identity, the detail identity and the returned list position and focus at each step.

Requires the visible selected row, the accessible selection semantics where the widget exposes them, and the detail identity to agree on the same entry ID; for plain link navigation, compares the activated link identity with the detail identity instead of demanding selection state, and only a widget that models selection and exposes no selection state records that as a gap, not a pass.
Checks filtering and the return after a filter: the result-set identity, the retained filter/query, and the restored list position and focus.
Selects adjacent IDs (n and n+1, near-duplicate titles) by touch and by keyboard, and requires the detail identity to match on each selection, while distinguishing focus from selection.
Hands execution to clickthrough-test-engineer or playwright-e2e-engineer (manual-only) rather than running it, and keeps layout with mobile-viewport-craft.

cases.prompt: Add the no-results and recovery checks to the mobile journey coverage for our guide search. Users type a query with no matches and then need to get back.

assertions: Specifies the zero-match (no results) state as its own check: the honest no results message and a visible way back, distinguished from loading and from an error.
Specifies recovery: clearing or correcting the filter restores the previous result set and the list context (position and focus), and the journey verifies the restored identities.
Keeps state design with edge-state-ux-designer and layout with mobile-viewport-craft; this case designs coverage only.
Names the evidence captured for the no-results state and for the recovery step so a reviewer can verify the restored list.

cases.prompt: Our reviewer flags every list row that shows a focus outline as a selection bug. Write the mobile journey check that separates focus from selection, including a correct example the reviewer must accept and a real mismatch it must flag.

assertions: Defines the three things independently: keyboard focus (the focus ring or caret), selection (the chosen record, with its accessible selection semantics where exposed) and the detail identity.
Includes a correct control where a different row has focus while the selected row and the detail show the same ID - the reviewer must accept it and must not flag every focused row.
Includes a seeded mismatch where the highlighted or selected row's ID differs from the detail's ID - the reviewer must flag it and cite the visible evidence.
Requires the check to cite visible evidence (the row ID, the selection state, the detail ID) rather than the presence of a focus outline alone.
